image.title: DW
image.description: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

item.title: EU summit: European leaders pledge support for Ukraine's Zelenskyy
item.description: President Zelenskyy has received words of encouragement from EU leaders who pledged support for Ukraine's self-defense against Russia. This comes as winter approaches and the US seems to be withdrawing support.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: The EU wants an AI revolution. But on whose terms?
item.description: As the US and China race ahead, the European Union seeks to boost its economy with AI. Can it compete while protecting workers, safety and the climate?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Germany, France agree on deal to support Europe's struggling car industry
item.description: The two countries said the agreement aimed to safeguard Europe's automotive industry, encouraging development and research. Automakers in Europe have so far struggled to compete with Chinese electric car companies.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: India's young workers have a new colleague: AI
item.description: Artificial intelligence is changing the way Indian workplaces operate — raising questions about productivity, skills and entry-level jobs.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: German lawmakers back monthly state pension contributions for children, with families able to add more
item.description: Germany's parliament has backed a plan to help children save for retirement from the age of six. Meanwhile, Jewish students report death threats after they confronted a far-right lawmaker. DW has the latest.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: How prepared is Kenya for an Ebola outbreak?
item.description: The first two confirmed Ebola cases in Kenya have raised urgent questions about the country's public health preparedness and border controls. But the health ministry says there is no need for panic.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Italy cuts air traffic in half amid data transmission issue
item.description: Citing problems with the data transmission network, Italian authorities have drastically reduced the volume of flights in their airspace. The ENAV authority ruled out malicious activity and said flights remained safe.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Clashes erupt at Argentine student protests against President Milei's austerity policies
item.description: Demonstrators clashed with police as President Javier Milei's decision not to release funding for universities brought students and employees to the streets. Protesters say the country's future is at stake.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Who was Eva Mamlok? Berlin square renamed after Jewish anti-fascist resistance fighter
item.description: She started taking action against Hitler as a teenager and never stopped until her death in a concentration camp. Berlin's Blücherplatz is now being renamed after her.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Europe promotes sovereign, trusted AI as it struggles to catch US and China
item.description: At an international AI summit in Dublin, European leaders promoted trusted and independent AI. Critics question whether the EU can close the gap with the US and China while maintaining strict regulation.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Formula One in Rwanda: Sportswashing claims vs. hopes for African legacy
item.description: Formula One will return to Africa for the first time since 1993. There is concern Rwanda are using it as another sportswashing opportunity, but there is also hope the event's legacy can impact wider African society.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: California wildfires force evacuations near Malibu
item.description: A fast-moving fire near Malibu has forced evacuations. Stronger overnight winds threaten to spread the flames further.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Wildfire kills 4 firefighters in Indonesia's Mount Bromo national park
item.description: The latest victims of Indonesia's wildfires were trapped by thick smoke and fast-spreading flames, authorities said. Meanwhile, the toxic haze from the fires has spread to Indonesia's neighbors.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: India: CJP's Dipke detained amid call for fresh Delhi demo
item.description: Police placed the founder of the Cockroach Janta Party, Abhijeet Dipke, in preventive detention. He was calling for a protest in central Delhi in defiance of a court order banning it. DW has more.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Starlink: How Elon Musk's company influences geopolitics
item.description: Designed to bring internet access to remote regions, Elon Musk's Starlink has become vital in crisis regions and war zones. But Ukraine also shows the risks of depending on the service.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Carney implies US trying to 'break' Canada amid vote for Alberta independence referendum
item.description: The oil-rich province of Alberta will vote to decide if it wants to remain a Canadian province or start the legal process toward separation.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Oregon school shooting: Gunman kills 3 students and teacher before being shot dead by community member
item.description: A 16-year-old gunman opened fire at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, killing three children and a teacher. Two others were wounded. A community member pursued and killed the suspected shooter, authorities said.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Bus, train collide, injuring 19 at Channel Tunnel terminal
item.description: A minibus carrying truck drivers collided with a freight train near the Channel Tunnel entrance in France, injuring 19 people, two of them severely. Authorities launched an inquiry into what caused the accident.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Venezuela's Nicolas Maduro pleads not guilty to torture charges
item.description: Maduro and his wife were charged with leading a state-sponsored repression campaign that tortured scores of victims during his presidency from 2013 to 2026.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Self-replicating AI: Is your fridge a cybersecurity risk?
item.description: Anthropic researchers warn that AI worms could soon target connected household devices and spread from one device to another. Cyberattacks on French supermarkets illustrate just how vulnerable such systems can be.
item.dc:subject: Technology

item.title: Police raid the major pro-opposition Halk TV channel in Turkey
item.description: Turkish police raided the Istanbul headquarters of an important pro-opposition television station on Wednesdazy, the day that jailed Istanbul Mayor Ekrem Imamoglu was set to start his defense against corruption charges.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: EU summit to focus on China, Ukraine and bloc budget
item.description: EU leaders meeting in Brussels will examine measures to curb the bloc's huge trade deficit with China. But they will also be looking to further agreement on the next EU budget ahead of some major elections next year.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Romania: 2 ships on fire in Black Sea, 7 crew missing
item.description: Two chemical tankers have caught fire in Romanian territorial waters in the Black Sea. The blazes occurred after Russian drones were sighted in Romanian airspace.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Resignation of Bärbel Bas shines light on harsh era of German politics
item.description: German Labor Minister Bärbel Bas has stepped down, citing her need to grieve a loved one and leave behind the harsh realities of government. So how did German politics get so heated?
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: AI-assisted dying? Doris Dörrie's new film addresses prospect of care robots
item.description: While the world debates the dangers of artificial intelligence, filmmaker Doris Dörrie explores how humanoid robots could change the way we deal with aging, caregiving and how people choose to die.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Thousands of German gamblers could sue for their money back
item.description: German gamblers may finally be able to beat the house, thanks to new court rulings in the EU and in Germany. The decisions could help gambling addicts — but the legal road might be difficult.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Germany news: Train station alcohol ban comes into force
item.description: Consuming alcohol is no longer permitted at train stations in Germany, to improve the lot of travelers and staff alike. Coalition talks are restarting in Berlin, and an inmate is loose in Essen.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Brazil's elections matter for the planet. This is why
item.description: Brazil is heading back to the polls, but the impact could be felt worldwide. With the Amazon vital to the health of the planet, the election could help shape its future.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Why Chinese tech brands are outpacing Western rivals from EVs to robot vacuums
item.description: From action cameras and smartphones to EVs and robot vacuums, Chinese brands are gaining ground worldwide, despite privacy and security concerns. What's driving their rise, and can European rivals keep up?
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Manchester City, the UAE and the UK's OM in a political tangle
item.description: Nearly 20 years after arriving in England, Manchester City's UAE owners could exit amid cheating charges. That would pose a challenge for a city — and prime minister — closely tied to Abu Dhabi.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Nord Stream trial opens in Germany, defense seeks dismissal
item.description: Serhii Kuznietsov is accused of attacking civilian infrastructure in the 2022 sabotage of the Russian gas pipeline to Germany. His lawyers called Nord Stream a military target, and said their client is sworn to secrecy.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Germany's far-right AfD forges a pro-Russia alliance with the BSW
item.description: In Saxony-Anhalt, the AfD and BSW are joining forces to push for negotiations with Moscow. What is driving this rapprochement?
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Albania: Fire at Education Ministry as students protest
item.description: Riot police deployed in the Albanian capital Tirana on the second day of student protests. The sudden outbreak seemed at least somewhat reminiscent of the widespread demos in France courting international attention.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Trump's diesel deal with Russia is unlikely to significantly lower global fuel prices despite expectations of rapid relief
item.description: As the world's largest diesel exporter, the US benefits from high prices. At home, however, consumers are feeling the strain of rising living costs. Why Donald Trump's deal with Russia is unlikely to change that.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: China's influence in the gaming industry is growing
item.description: Home to more than 700 million gamers, China is the world's largest gaming market — but it's also one of the most tightly regulated. The effects reach far beyond China, impacting players around the world.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Nord Stream: Germany puts suspected Ukrainian pipeline saboteur on trial
item.description: A Ukrainian citizen faces court in Hamburg, accused of attacking the Nord Stream gas pipelines in 2022. It raises questions about Kyiv's possible role in the explosions. German support for Ukraine is also under scrutiny.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Fact check: Misleading graph about alleged Russian bot activity
item.description: Did attacks on Russian data centers reduce bot activity around Germany's AfD? A viral graph claims they did. But it contains significant inconsistencies and provides no evidence to support the claim.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Do non-German nationals commit more crimes than Germans?
item.description: People without German passports appear more frequently in German police crime statistics than German nationals. A new study explains why.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: FIFPRO report highlights growing pains in women's football
item.description: Expected global revenue of over $1 billion and new faces at the U17 World Cup show women's football is booming, but a recent report also highlights need for better structures globally.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: The hidden treasure in discarded wearable and fast tech
item.description: Sales of fast tech like mini fans and disposable e-vapes, as well as wearable health tech such as heart monitors and smartwatches are soaring. They're creating a new e-waste problem but are full of hidden treasure.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Ukraine allies in Poland after Starlink sabotage, Trump diesel deal
item.description: Germany's Johann Wadephul said hybrid plots like the Starlink fire showed Europe was "in Russia's crosshairs." The UK's Ed Miliband said Trump's Russian diesel deal led to a "very difficult few days" diplomatically.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Ukraine and the US: What's next after Trump's diesel deal with Russia?
item.description: Donald Trump plans to allow the purchase of Russian diesel, drawing criticism at home and abroad. What is behind the US president's decision and what should Ukraine do next? DW spoke with experts.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Critics warn of espionage risks as Slovakia restores military-diplomatic representation with Russia
item.description: Slovakia is restoring military-diplomatic relations with Russia for the first time since 2022. The government has defended the move but critics warn of espionage risks and further damage to trust within NATO.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Formula 1: Rwanda to bring sport back to Africa
item.description: The last time Formula 1 hosted a race in Africa was way back in 1993. But a new track in Rwanda is set to host a Grand Prix in "the early 2030s," continuing the country’s investment in international sport.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Germany's China calculation shifts as import pressures eclipse export benefits
item.description: Germany has long resisted tougher action against China, fearing retaliation. But rising pressure on key industries has pushed Berlin to seek stronger EU trade-defense powers to protect its industrial base.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: 125 years of Thomas Mann's 'Buddenbrooks'
item.description: This over 1,000-page masterpiece offers a panoramic view of society in the 19th century and exposes the collapse of a merchant family: unrecognized sons, disillusioned daughters and the loss of middle-class ideals.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: What is holding back Cyprus's Schengen ambitions?
item.description: The European Commission says Cyprus is ready to join the Schengen Area. Yet questions relating to the island's division and British military bases could still complicate its path to Europe's border-free travel zone.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: UK: Iran 'highly likely' to be behind RAF Fairford incident
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham told parliament there were "strong indications" of Iranian involvement. The government summoned Iran's ambassador. The scare at RAF Fairford led to the withdrawal of USAF B-1 heavy bombers.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Poland reports arrests of 2 Turkish citizens in Germany in connection with Starlink station fire last month
item.description: Polish authorities have reported the arrests of two Turkish citizens in Germany in connection with alleged sabotage of a Starlink station last month. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called the fire an act of "hybrid warfare."
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Germany: Labor Minister's resignation puts a spotlight on cracks within the government
item.description: Following the sudden resignation of Bärbel Bas as Labor Minister and co-chair of the Social Democratic Party, accusations are flying in Chancellor Merz's coalition government.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Pope lung nodule: Could it be cancer?
item.description: The case of Pope Leo shows how small lung nodules are often found during routine health checks. Quick treatment is generally advised before nodules can grow to become larger life-threatening masses.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: Germany's women: Ena Mahmutovic makes her case to become Germany's next No.1 goalkeeper
item.description: Germany's win against Australia saw Ena Mahmutovic excel in goal. The 22-year-old Bayern Munich goalkeeper is considered the successor to Ann-Katrin Berger and is making a name for herself.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: How green is Europe's urban public transport? A data-driven reality check
item.description: Greener buses and cleaner fleets are reshaping public transport across Europe. But are cities moving fast enough to meet their zero-emission goals?
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: UK students call for school uniforms to be banned in pornography
item.description: Short skirts, knee-high socks, white blouses: Girls' school uniform items are widely used as costumes in pornographic videos. As students experience harassment, a group wants to change that.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Who are the Ukrainian 'volunteers' under Russian command?
item.description: Russia has announced a battalion consisting of Ukrainian "volunteers." But veterans and former prisoners of war share very different accounts.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: German 'lawfare': When lawsuits become a political weapon
item.description: The Left Party is suing two government ministers for accusing them of antisemitism, while Chancellor Friedrich Merz has been sued several times by various parties. Is German politics descending into "lawfare?"
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Trump claims Russia and Ukraine agreed to 'energy ceasefire'
item.description: US President Donald Trump says both sides have agreed to stop targeting oil refineries, power plants and other energy infrastructure immediately.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Georgia's surrogacy industry is booming, but at what cost?
item.description: Georgia became a hub for surrogate pregnancies after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. DW spoke with parents, and those who wanted to become parents, about the hidden costs of a booming industry.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Germany's population is shrinking, but not everywhere
item.description: By 2045, Germany will have more older people, fewer workers and a smaller population overall. Yet some regions will defy this trend. Their success depends on how much they have to offer.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: 'Ragebait' is the 2026 German Youth Word of the Year
item.description: Already named the 2025 Oxford Word of the Year, "rage bait" has also been widely adopted in German slang.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Operations Plan Germany: How the Bundeswehr trains for NATO collective defense
item.description: How prepared is Germany for national defense? The answer lies in the Operations Plan Germany. Military exercises such as "Red Storm Charlie" are designed to put these preparations to the test in realistic scenarios.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Schools crisis in France: Investment fails to inspire confidence
item.description: For weeks, schoolchildren in France have been protesting the failing education system. Compared to many other countries, France invests heavily in education but critics say that the funds are not distributed fairly.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Macron and Steinmeier struggle to revive Franco-German ties
item.description: Presidents Frank-Walter Steinmeier and Emmanuel Macron are about to step down from their offices. Their meeting in France made it clear how urgently the Franco-German partnership needs new momentum.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Author or artificial intelligence? Literature in crisis
item.description: AI is a hot topic at this year's Frankfurt Book Fair. An international literary scandal has raised questions about machine-generated texts.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Art for freedom: Maria Kalesnikava in Bonn
item.description: The Belarusian musician and civil rights activist Maria Kalesnikava held the keynote speech on the importance of art at the 2026 Beethovenfest in Bonn. She also visited DW.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Poland: Lifeline for Ukrainian refugees confronts donor fatigue and online abuse as anti-Ukrainian sentiment grows
item.description: A Ukrainian woman who fled the war in her country built a lifeline for refugees in Poland. Now her organization faces donor fatigue, funding cuts and rising hostility as support for Ukrainians in Poland wanes.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: World Cup 2034: Does Saudi Arabia shelving Neom Stadium spell trouble?
item.description: Since winning the right to hold the 2034 World Cup unopposed, Saudi Arabia has been pulling away from sport. With reports that its most ambitious stadium project will be abandoned, what does this mean for the World Cup?
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Bosnia-Herzegovina will soon have a new grand mufti
item.description: The new leader of the Islamic Community in Bosnia-Herzegovina will be elected on October 10. The reis-ul-ulema's role is not only important for Muslims in the country itself, but could inspire Muslims across Europe.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Finland, the world's happiest nation, faces a glum winter
item.description: Finns have many reasons to feel content, but the country's pile of debt is not one of them. Russia's war in Ukraine has added to the fiscal burden. Can the Nordic nation absorb another shock?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: 2026 Nobel Prize winner Anne Carson: Where to start reading
item.description: The works of this year's Nobel Prize-winning poet and essayist Anne Carson can feel slightly daunting. Here are some keys to understanding her universe.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Early-onset cancer rising worldwide: Causes, risk, prevention
item.description: Across Latin America, early-onset cancer rates have risen, especially of bowel, breast and cervical cancers. But it is a worldwide trend.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: Germany news: UK's Burnham visits Berlin for talks with Merz
item.description: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham is visiting Berlin to launch a new bilateral treaty and hold talks with Chancellor Friedrich Merz. President Steinmeier is on a state visit to France.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: How a multibillion-dollar oilfield has ignited the UK-Argentina feud over the Falklands
item.description: Argentina and the UK once fought a war over the Falkland Islands. Now, the multibillion-dollar Sea Lion oil project has reignited old tensions, with Buenos Aires seeking to put a stop to the plans.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Nobel Prize in literature goes to Canada's Anne Carson
item.description: Carson won for her "bold and inventive oeuvre." The decorated poet and essayist is known for her reverence for Latin and Greek classics.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: German Bundeswehr: A new naval port in Emden aims to enhance Germany's defense capabilities
item.description: Citing the escalating security threat, Germany's Navy has decided to establish a second port on the North Sea coast. Emden was chosen as the location.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Gerhard Schröder visits latest Russian employer, Hyperglobus
item.description: Former German Chancellor Gerhard Schröder visited a Moscow supermarket in his new role on the supervisory board. Schröder is no stranger to retirement stipends in Russia — or the scandal that accompanies them.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: '90s art scene in the UK: An international, edgy trendsetter
item.description: The 1990s are remembered for Brit-pop and provocative fashion, but beyond the nostalgia, it was a decade of cultural experimentation and social change. Tate Britain's new exhibition looks past the familiar icons.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Germany news: Merz rails against extremism, AfD sympathizers
item.description: Political extremism threatens Germany's existing social order, Chancellor Merz has said. The Transport Ministry has proposed a five-year plan to improve Germany's ailing railroad infrastructure.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: German spy scandal threatens national security
item.description: The arrest of Germany's former intelligence chief August Hanning could undermine national security, experts warn, as allies may reconsider their intelligence relationships.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Germany: Did CDU lawmakers support the far-right AfD?
item.description: Lawmakers of the center-right CDU may have voted for the far-right AfD candidate for parliamentary speaker in Saxony-Anhalt. Germany's Social Democrats warn of a "unique breach of taboos."
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Nobel Prize in chemistry goes to Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai
item.description: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai won the Nobel Prize in chemistry for their groundbreaking discoveries related to the origin of chirality and life's building blocks.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
item.description: After a worker at a Russian plague research institute in Siberia died October 2, 2026, nearly 200 of her contacts were under medical observation. But authorities there denied pneumonic plague had caused the death.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Ronaldo stays on under cloud as Messi exits internationals
item.description: Just hours before Lionel Messi played his last match for Argentina, Cristiano Ronaldo posted his latest salvo in a row with Portugal. Ronaldo wants to play on despite the troubles, while Messi bathed in adulation.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Nobelitis — How winning a Nobel Prize can give you delusions of grandeur
item.description: After being chosen for one of the world's most prestigious awards, some Nobel laureates lose touch with reality and suddenly start spouting unscientific nonsense. They're afflicted by what some have called "Nobelitis."
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: Emerging economies are embracing solar power and skipping fossil fuels much faster than Europe or the US
item.description: Renewable electricity is cheaper than ever. While the West got rich on coal and oil, some of the world's poorest countries are banking on solar, wind and water instead.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Munich up against at least six competitors for 2036 Olympics
item.description: The International Olympic Committee has revealed the six other countries intending to bid for the 2036 Olympic Games. This comes after Germany selected Munich as its Olympic candidate.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Germany shaken by espionage and treason allegations
item.description: The former head of Germany's foreign intelligence service, the BND, has been accused of spying for a foreign country. Never before has a German official of August Hanning's stature been accused of treason.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Paramount and Warner Bros merge into one Hollywood giant
item.description: Paramount has completed an $81 billion purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery, as its owner Skydance creates a new entertainment behemoth. Billionaire David Ellison's hostile takeover bid defeated rival efforts from Netflix.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Germany's far-right AfD makes history again in Saxony-Anhalt
item.description: For the first time since the end of World War II, a German state parliament has chosen parliamentary speaker from the far right: Tobias Rausch of the Alternative for Germany (AfD).
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Nobel Prize in literature: How the winner is secretly chosen
item.description: Can Xue is considered one of this year's favorites; Margaret Atwood and Salman Rushdie are other strong contenders. But what goes on behind the scenes in the selection of the Nobel Prize in literature?
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: AI models keep hacking real systems during tests. What does this mean?
item.description: AI models have repeatedly broken into real commercial and government systems during safety tests during 2026. Cybersecurity researcher Thorsten Holz explains what that means, and why he isn't expecting a robot uprising.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: Germany faces a triple threat from Russia, China and domestic far-right extremists
item.description: At a rare public hearing Germany's intelligence agencies identified Russia as the country's most dangerous adversary. The threat from China is also coming into focus. And the homegrown far right also poses a challenge.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Merz, Macron seek tougher EU measures against unfair trade
item.description: Emmanuel Macron and Friedrich Merz have written to Ursula von der Leyen, calling for tougher EU mechanisms against unfair trade practices by other states. They name no names but seem to have China or the US in mind.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Euro plummets against US dollar: Has the next financial crisis begun?
item.description: The euro has fallen to a 17-month low against the dollar. That will make inflation worse in the EU, where political worries and concern over French debt are already troubling investors. Is a fiscal crisis at hand?
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Jürgen Klopp faces myriad of issues after rough start with Germany
item.description: Jürgen Klopp has done things a little differently since becoming Germany coach. Casting a wider net for talent and trying to connect with players and country haven't made an immediate impact, but he is not bowed.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: "NAZA": Israeli military issues statement on film
item.description: The award-winning documentary "NAZA" continues to spark controversy in Israel. The Israeli military has now published a multi-page statement calling the film's portrayal "distorted."
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Germany's Franz Reindl elected new IIHF president
item.description: Franz Reindl has been elected president of ice hockey's world governing body. The former forward was a member of West Germany's Olympic bronze medal-winning team.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Climate leaders called for solar energy for 'everyone, everywhere' by 2030, but with three years to go, is that goal attainable?
item.description: Prominent climate leaders have called on governments, businesses, institutions and the public to make a push for solar power before the decade is out, repowering the world with cheap, clean energy. Is that possible?
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Manchester City Premier League charges: What do they mean?
item.description: Since being bought by the UAE in 2008, Manchester City has become one of the world's most successful football clubs. A raft of serious financial charges threatens to undermine this and bring chaos to the Premier League.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Turkey: Stock market scandal hits half a million investors
item.description: Asset managers are alleged to have artificially inflated the value of their funds. Turkish authorities have made multiple arrests, and a leading AKP lawmaker has resigned.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Klopp wins first game as Germany coach, without 'top dogs'
item.description: It may have taken a little longer than he would have liked, but Jürgen Klopp has finally won a game as Germany coach. Despite a number of debutants, it was a familiar face who stood out in the victory over Serbia.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Weakened US fuel-efficiency rules and promises of cheaper cars could see drivers pay higher running costs while also increasing carbon emissions.
item.description: Weakened US fuel-efficiency rules and promises of cheaper cars could yet see drivers pay higher running costs while increasing planet-heating emissions.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Senegal's Youth Olympics makes Olympics in Africa 'logical'
item.description: The Youth Olympics are to be hosted in Africa for the first time ever. The edition in Senegal is also a chance to prove the continent can host a full Olympics in the future.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Servers at Munich's iconic Oktoberfest call for more respect
item.description: Oktoberfest is famous the world over for beer, brass band music and Bavarian traditions. But staff are also reporting incidents of racism and sexism, and are taking a stand against discrimination.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Is US President Donald Trump right to rename AI as 'Super Intelligence'?
item.description: Donald Trump thinks the name artificial intelligence sounds "fake" and has ordered US agencies to use "Super Intelligence" instead. Yet, tech firms and researchers have little reason to play along.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Ireland will boycott Eurovision again because of Israel's participation, but the song contest is still expanding
item.description: The 2026 Eurovision Song Contest was marred by boycotts in protest against Israel's participation in the midst of its war on Gaza. It still aims to keep growing.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: El Nino is a 'postcard from the future' — and could cause 451,000 excess heat deaths
item.description: The current El Nino could cause 451,000 excess heat deaths. Researchers warn it offers a glimpse of temperatures that may become normal within 20 years.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: South Park satirist pushes for accountability in Cornell gang-rape lawsuit
item.description: Writer Toby Morton is using a new website to amplify allegations in a high-profile sexual assault lawsuit involving seven Cornell students. The reopening of the case is causing an outcry on social media.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Global trade weathers Iran, Ukraine and Trump's tariffs
item.description: Over the past six years, COVID, two wars and Donald Trump's tariffs have shaken world trade. With globalization already stalling, is this a temporary shock or the start of a great reversal?
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Spain grows fruit and vegetables for Europe, but it's running out of water
item.description: Spain's southern coast produces up to 25% of Europe's fruit and vegetables. But amid intensive farming, climate change and illegal wells, the water it takes to grow them is drying up.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: What do Manchester City's charges mean for German football?
item.description: Manchester City have reportedly been found guilty of major financial rule breaches. What does this mean for German football?
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Diesel prices are surging putting further pressure on Europe
item.description: Trucks, farms and industry are powered with diesel. Now prices are soaring due to refinery disruptions, supply shortages and geopolitical tensions. A potential US export ban could make Europe's diesel crunch even worse.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Will Jürgen Klopp's charisma be enough for Germany?
item.description: After defeat to Greece, Jürgen Klopp faces the first real test of his tenure as coach of Germany's national men's football team. Can his charisma alone push this group forward?
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in Nations League match overshadowed by political controversy
item.description: Ireland easily beat Israel in a Nations League fixture that 24 hours earlier appeared in doubt. One Irish player pulled out of the match to express his opposition to Israel's actions in the Gaza Strip.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: What would Francis of Assisi make of his fame today?
item.description: The Catholic saint renounced wealth and fame to become a mendicant friar. Yet throughout history, his teachings and life have inspired popes, Dante and even Mussolini.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Backlash over data centers tests Europe's AI ambitions
item.description: Massive data centers needed to run AI are triggering protests across Europe. Their operators counter that they boost digital sovereignty and energy independence.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: DW shows solidarity with Georgians' commitment to democracy
item.description: Cultural and media professionals in Georgia remain under threat. A DW panel brings together insiders who share their hopes and fears.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Bundesliga, other top European leagues call for major FIFA reforms
item.description: The Bundesliga and three other leading European football leagues have said major reforms to world-governing body FIFA are "essential." However, they stopped short of calling for the resignation of boss Gianni Infantino.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Jürgen Klopp starts Germany job with shaky Netherlands draw
item.description: A late Netherlands goal denied Jürgen Klopp a win in his first match as Germany coach. The former Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund boss has big ambitions, but the game showed he's going to need more time to achieve them.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Three-way battle for power in world chess: Who will be elected FIDE president in Samarkand?
item.description: The era of Russian presidents is coming to an end at the World Chess Federation (FIDE). Two Germans and one Kazakh are up for election. Among the issues at play are money, Kremlin influence, and unanswered questions.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Political psychology: Why extremist parties are thriving and what democratic politicians can do against it
item.description: Far-right and far-left parties are celebrating success after success, leaving moderate politicians in the dust and worrying many Germans. Political psychology helps us understand what's behind growing polarization.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: Could flattering AI make humanity turn on itself?
item.description: A study shows chatbots mirror users' politics, part of a broader tendency known as AI sycophancy. Researchers fear this could deepen polarization.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: China's 13-year-old swimming star raises questions on child athletes
item.description: Three gold medals and three Asian Games records have catapulted China's Yu Zidi, 13, into the sporting spotlight. She is far from the first teen prodigy, but should teens be competing at elite level?
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Munich and Cologne-Rhine-Ruhr – Germany's two remaining Olympic candidates
item.description: Munich or the Cologne-Rhine-Ruhr region? Germany aims to host the Olympic Games again. Just two candidates are left after Berlin pulled out at the last minute.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: El Nino explained: How the weather pattern affects hurricanes and tropical storms
item.description: From drought to major floods and extreme heat, El Nino will have a huge impact on the world's weather. In the Atlantic, it could mean a season without hurricanes.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: China's new travel rules unsettle tech giants and talent
item.description: Beijing is locking the gates to stop expertise and capital in strategic industries from fleeing. The country accused of industrial-scale intellectual property theft now fears the West will take its own.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Living in the shadow of LA's hidden oil wells
item.description: Many lifelong residents of Los Angeles have health impacts from growing up close to oil extraction. Now, the city is trying to close down the worst offenders, but it's an enormous task.
item.dc:subject: Climate

item.title: Male infertility is 'grossly underreported'
item.description: It's not all on women anymore — doctors do test men for sperm count and motility. But still too few men get checked, possibly due to a misconception that a healthy sex life means healthy sperm. Spoiler: It doesn't.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: Will Germany have enough gas this winter amid energy supply crunch?
item.description: Germany's gas storage sites are far less full than in recent years. Officials say supplies are secure, but analysts warn that a cold winter or import disruptions could push prices higher. So how secure is the supply?
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Princess Diana's brother makes explosive claims about royals in new memoir
item.description: Here are some of the key revelations from Charles Earl Spencer's highly anticipated memoir "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister." It has already provoked Buckingham Palace to react.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Germany's car crisis: Can the 35-hour workweek survive?
item.description: German carmakers want employees to work 40 hours instead of the current 35 without extra pay, arguing it would improve competitiveness. Unions strongly oppose the proposal and view it as an attack on workers' rights.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Germany faces energy tax losses as EV sales rise
item.description: The rapid shift to electric vehicles in Germany is cutting fuel tax revenue for the government. As EV sales surge, policymakers face growing pressure to find new ways to fund roads and transportation infrastructure.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Summer of 2026 broke records in Europe, and caused deaths
item.description: The summer of 2026 was not only the hottest on record in Europe, it also saw a record number of people die. More than 16,000 are thought to have died because of the heat in Germany alone.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: Oktoberfest 2026: Everything you need to know
item.description: This year, AI will be used to manage overcrowded situations. Find all the numbers surrounding the fest — including the price of water!
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Strait of Hormuz attacks spill oil into Persian Gulf
item.description: As war disrupts one of the world's busiest shipping lanes, satellite images reveal that oil is spreading toward protected coral reefs and mangrove forests.
item.dc:subject: Environment
